summary: Aggregate latency spike caused by client SDK retry amplification against silent quota enforcement
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightHealthAI reported intermittent but sustained inference slowdowns and request timeouts for live traffic hitting rw-llm-large-v1 in us-east. Initial symptom: spikes in p95/p99 latency and a rise in perceived client-side timeouts.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints for BrightHealthAI experienced higher tail latency starting 2026-03-11 21:00 UTC, with cascading 5xx/timeout observations from their frontend.
- Customer reports degraded user experience and several aborted sessions. Estimated ~12% request failure for the last 12 hours for the tenant.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod (us-east), running rw-llm-large-v1 pinned to model:v2026-02-28.
- Customer using internal SDK (v0.9.2) with default retry settings (immediate retry ramp, no jitter).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Send a burst of concurrent streaming generation requests (20-50/sec) from their service using SDK v0.9.2.
2. Observe initial 429 responses followed by client-side timeouts and long-tail latency.
3. When retry storms occur, end-to-end p95 jumps >3x and many requests fail with timeout on the client.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side metrics: rising queue length at the API gateway, increased connection churn, and elevated CPU on serving nodes.
- Rate-limiter observed a growth in 429 responses for the tenant; however, some 429 responses lacked a Retry-After header in the path used by the Dedicated control plane.
- Customer SDK treats non-2xx as a transient network error and immediately retries without respecting Retry-After; retries have no jitter which concentrates load.

Expected behavior:
- Clients should respect Retry-After or backoff headers and include randomized jitter; server should return clear Retry-After when imposing quota enforcement.

Initial logs and evidence:
- Observability dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/tenants/BrightHealthAI/latency (private link).
- Sample gateway logs: repeated identical request IDs from the same tenant IP over short intervals; p99 request duration rose from 420ms -> 1.9s during amplification window.
- Rate-limiter trace: tokens exhausted at 2026-03-11T21:03:15Z followed by an increase of 429s for the tenant. Some enforcement paths returned 429 without body headers due to a fallback path in dedicated control-plane code (seen in logs).
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Thompson: Customer opened ticket. Provided initial traces and example request IDs. Marked P1 due to user-facing SLA impact.
2026-03-12 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Acknowledged and requested full request/response capture and SDK version. Asked customer to reduce concurrency as a temporary mitigation.
2026-03-12 - BrightHealthAI (Sarah Lee): Confirmed they were on SDK v0.9.2 and will try lowering concurrency; reported immediate improvement but issue returned when traffic resumed.

2026-03-13 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Correlated tenant traffic pattern with 429 spike. Noted missing Retry-After on some enforcement responses from dedicated control plane; created internal task INT-987 to track fix.

2026-03-13 - Dev (Priya Nair): Reproduced locally with SDK v0.9.2. Observed client retries stacking without jitter; opened PR to add client-side default jitter and Retry-After awareness in next SDK patch.
2026-03-14 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Applied temporary per-tenant ingress circuit breaker to limit retry amplification. Instructed customer to upgrade SDK to v0.10.0-beta (patched backoff).
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: Combination of (1) dedicated-plane quota enforcement returning 429s inconsistently (some enforcement paths lacked Retry-After header) and (2) customer SDK treating 429 as retriable network error with no jitter. This produced a retry amplification loop increasing load and tail latency.
Metrics show a tight correlation between the start of repeated identical request IDs and a rapid increase in queue depth -> p99 latency -> downstream timeouts in the customer's frontend.

A small code path in the dedicated control plane falls back to a generic enforcement response which didn't include Retry-After; affected tenants only when specific quota buckets were hit (explains why not all customers were impacted).
SDK replay confirmed that immediate retries double/triple request rate within seconds and can overwhelm tenant pool even when absolute QPS is modest.
No evidence of model runtime bug; serving nodes remained healthy once ingress load was throttled.
Relevant logs: gateway trace IDs [gw:0a3f, gw:0b7c, gw:0d21] show 8-12 repeated attempts per initial request from same client within <5s.
Related tickets: SUP-84217 highlighted 429s misinterpreted by clients (useful context) but this case differs due to a missing Retry-After header path in dedicated control plane.
resolution: Short-term mitigation (2026-03-14): Applied tenant-level ingress circuit breaker to cap immediate retries for BrightHealthAI. This reduced p95/p99 within 20 minutes of activation.

Customer action: BrightHealthAI agreed to upgrade to SDK v0.10.0-beta which implements Retry-After handling and randomized exponential backoff. They deployed the change to canary services and reported reduced retry storms.

Medium-term fix (planned): Deploy forced Retry-After header from all quota enforcement paths in the dedicated control plane (INT-987). Add server-side per-tenant token bucket to smooth bursts and return clear headers. Target rollout: 2026-03-21 behind feature flag.

Long-term: Update SDK docs and default settings to encourage conservative retry behavior; add automated detection/alerting for retry amplification patterns per tenant in the console (post-incident task assigned to Observability team).
Follow-up tasks: INT-987 (dedicated control plane header bug), INT-1024 (observability alert for retry amplification), DEV-PR-456 (SDK backoff/jitter default).
next_steps: Track INT-987 to completion and coordinate deployment with Dedicated infra team.
Confirm BrightHealthAI completes SDK upgrade across all their services and monitor for recurrence for 72 hours post-rollout.
Add a short KB article for customers on recommended retry strategies and SDK versions. (Docs owner: Developer Experience)
Postmortem: schedule 1-hour blameless postmortem with SRE, Dedicated infra, DevEx, and the customer for week of 2026-03-22.
Update ticket with final closure details once INT tasks are resolved and customer confirms stability.
